name: Kingdom of Burma (Konbaung dynasty)
native: ကုန်းဘောင် (Konbaung)

predecessors.name: Konbaung dynasty
predecessors.text: the Konbaung realm of Bodawpaya (reigned 1782-1819), which Cliopatria carries on unchanged as 'Burma' from 1820

successors.name: British Raj
successors.text: Upper Burma, annexed to British India: 'Burma was annexed by the British on January 1, 1886, by the proclamation of the Viceroy and Governor-General of India'

ledger.x: 1820: Cliopatria's 'Burma' row begins, the Konbaung kingdom of Bodawpaya's successor.
1820: the Shan states are tributaries of the Burmese crown: Shan states paid tribute at various times, but unlike the Mon lands, they were never directly controlled by the Burmese.
1820: the Kachin hills are tributary fiefdoms: The Kachin, Palaung and Manipuri principalities were tributary fiefdoms, autonomous in practice.
1820: Manipur is a tributary fiefdom (the Kachin, Palaung and Manipuri principalities were tributary fiefdoms); Bodawpaya acquired Arakan, Manipur and Assam.
1821: the capital moves from Amarapura to Ava (Inwa), capital Ava, 1765-1783 and 1821-1842.
1824: the British enter Rangoon.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1825: Assam is lost: the Burmese were expelled from Assam in the summer of 1825; the Treaty of Yandabo confirmed the cession.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1825: the British invade Arakan.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1825: Arakan is lost.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1825: Arakan passes to the British: Mrauk-U fell on 1 April 1825 and the cession was confirmed at Yandabo (Burma ceded Assam, Arakan, and the Tenasserim coast).
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1826: the Treaty of Yandabo is signed on 24 February 1826.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1826: the war ends on 24 February 1826 with the treaty; the page does not say when the British left Rangoon, so the occupation is ended with the war.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1826: Manipur leaves Burmese suzerainty.
1842: the capital moves back from Ava to Amarapura (Amarapura, 1783-1821 and 1842-1857).
1852: the Second Anglo-Burmese War.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1853: the war ends 'without any treaty being signed', with the proclamation of annexation of 20 January 1853.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1853: Lower Burma is annexed by the British.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1857: Mindon's capital moves to Mandalay (Mandalay, 1857-1885).
1875: Mindon cedes the Karenni States.

1885: the Third Anglo-Burmese War opens on 7 November 1885 ('7-29 November 1885, with sporadic resistance continuing into 1887'), the British acting because they were 'alarmed by the consolidation of French Indochina'.
1885: Mandalay falls on 28 November and King Thibaw is taken prisoner; the king ordered his troops to lay down their arms.
1885: Upper Burma passes to British India.
1885: the Shan states leave Burmese suzerainty: the infobox says the 'Shan States became independent until the British incorporation into British India'.

1885: the Kachin principalities leave the Burmese crown with the kingdom's fall; the page says only that 'the British also extended their control into the tribal areas of the Kachin Hills and Chin Hills', without a date.
1885: the Konbaung kingdom ends: 'Following the war, Burma came under the rule of the British Raj as one of its provinces'; annexation proclaimed on 1 January 1886.

wars.name: First Anglo-Burmese War
wars.outcome: British victory: Treaty of Yandabo, 24 February 1826; Burma cedes Assam, Arakan and the Tenasserim coast, stops interfering in Cachar and Jaintia, pays one million pounds; Manipur independent (or British, the page conflicts).

wars.name: Second Anglo-Burmese War
wars.outcome: British victory without a treaty: Pegu (Lower Burma) annexed by proclamation on 20 January 1853; Pagan Min deposed by Mindon.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Burmese War
wars.outcome: British victory in 7-29 November 1885: Mandalay falls on 28 November, Thibaw taken prisoner; Burma annexed to British India on 1 January 1886.

certainty.note: Hill, Shan and Kachin frontiers are tributary and approximate; the cessions of Arakan and Tenasserim (Yandabo, 24 February 1826) and of Pegu (proclaimed 20 January 1853) are sharp as acts but no page opened gives the boundary line.
